summary: Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki (1870–1966) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Waseda University, the University of Tokyo, and under Kōsen Imakita, Soyen Shaku, and Paul Carus. He held professorships at Otani University (1921–1960) and Columbia University (1952–1957).

Daishun Ueyama (1934–2011) specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology, studying under Akira Fujieda. He spent his career at Ryukoku University as an associate professor (~1969–1978), professor (~1978–2004), and president (~1996–2000).

Daisy Cheung is a scholar in Indology and Tibetology. She earned degrees from the University of Hong Kong and a Ph.D. from the University of Hamburg (2012–2021), later becoming a postdoctoral research fellow at the Austrian Academy of Sciences in 2024.

Daito Shimaji (1875–1927) worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. After studying at Ryukoku and Otani universities, he taught at Toyo University (~1908–1927), Komazawa and Rissho universities (~1913–1927), and the University of Tokyo (1923).

Dale S. Wright (born 1948) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Alan Anderson, Wang Pachow, and Robert P. Scharlemann, and served as David B. and Mary H. Gamble Professor at Occidental College (~1980–2017).

Dalpat Rajpurohit specializes in Indology. He studied at Jai Narain Vyas University, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and Presidency University (Ph.D. 2014–2019). He lectured at Columbia University (2008–2018) before becoming Assistant Professor at the University of Texas at Austin in 2019.

Dalsukh Malvania (1910–2000) was an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar. He served as Director of the L.D. Institute of Indology (~1957–1977) and held positions at Banaras Hindu University, Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda, and the University of Toronto.
Damaru Chandra Bhatta is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He earned his PhD at Tribhuvan University and served as an Associate Professor at Tri-Chandra Multiple Campus in 1994.
Damchö Gyatso studied under Penor Rinpoche, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche.
Damdin Badaraev was active in Tibetology and linguistics, having studied under Bidia Dandaron and George de Roerich.

Damien Keown (born 1951) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Lancaster University and completed his D.Phil. at the University of Oxford (1986), later serving at Goldsmiths, University of London, including as Emeritus Professor (1995).

Damodar Dharmananda Kosambi (1907–1966) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Harvard University under George David Birkhoff and held mathematics professorships at Fergusson College (1932) and the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (1945–1962).

Dan Arnold (born 1965) specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago (~1997–2003) and held posts at McGill University (2003–2004) and the University of Chicago (2004–2011).
Dan Li specializes in linguistics and Buddhist studies. Having studied under Sherab Gyatso, they serve as an Associate Professor at Soka University (attested 2026).

Dan Lusthaus specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy, having earned a Ph.D. from Temple University under scholars including Bimal Krishna Matilal. He held posts at Grinnell College, Bates College, the University of Georgia, and Harvard University (2005).

Dan Martin (born 1953) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Ohio State, Kent State, and Indiana University Bloomington (Ph.D. 1991). He held positions at Swarthmore College, Carnegie Mellon, and the Hebrew University of Jerusalem.

Dan Smyer Yü works in religious studies and Tibetology. He completed a PhD at the University of California, Davis, and served as Research Group Leader at the Max Planck Institute for the Study of Religious and Ethnic Diversity.

Dan Zahavi (born 1967) is a philosopher who studied at KU Leuven under Rudolf Bernet and the University of Copenhagen. He has served as Professor of Philosophy at the University of Copenhagen (2002) and held a post at Oxford (2018–2021).

Daniel Aaron Getz works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his Ph.D. at Yale University under Stanley Weinstein, also studying under Ying-shih Yü and Tairyo Makita, and became an associate professor at Bradley University (attested 2019).
Daniel Amadé Scheidegger is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his doctoral degree at the University of Bristol under the supervision of Paul Williams.
